and & & & & & & & & & 2T = mg & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & & ...(ii)

Here, T is the tension in the string. Now, suppose A is further displaced by a distance x from its mean position and v be its speed at this moment. Then B lowers by $\dfrac{x}{2}$ and speed of B at this instant will be $\dfrac{v}{2}$ Total energy of the system in this position will be,

$\text{E} = \dfrac{1}{2} \text{k} {\left(x + {x}_{0}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} {m}_{A} v^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2} {m}_{B} {\left(\dfrac{\text{v}}{2}\right)}^{2} + {m}_{A} {gh}_{A} - {m}_{B} {gh}_{B}$

\dfrac{\text{d} \text{v}}{\text{dt}} =$ a$

\text{and} \text{k} {x}_{2} + \text{mg sin} \text{\theta} = \dfrac{\text{mg}}{2} \left[\text{From equations (i) and (ii)}\right]

\text{We get,} \dfrac{5}{4} $$\text{m}$$ a = - $$\text{k}$$ x$

questions.q: If the displacement $( x )$ and velocity $( v )$ of a particle executing SHM are related through the expression $3{v}^{2} = 30 - {x}^{2}$. If the time period of the particle is $T = \pi\sqrt{n}$, then what is the value of $n$?
questions.solution:
Given equation,

$3{v}^{2} = 30 - {x}^{2}$
Differentiating both sides, we get
$6v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = - 2x$

$⇒ v\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \dfrac{- 1}{3}x$

$⇒ \dfrac{a}{x} = \dfrac{- 1}{3} \ldots \left[∵ a = \dfrac{dv}{dt} = \dfrac{dv}{dx}\dfrac{dx}{dt} = v\dfrac{dv}{dx}\right]$

$T = \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\left|\dfrac{\text{acceleration}}{\text{displacement}}\right|}} = \dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{\left|\dfrac{- 1}{3}\right|}} = 2\pi\sqrt{3} = \pi\sqrt{12}$

$n = 12$

questions.solution:
Assuming the two pendulums follow the following functions of their displacement :

θ1 = θ0 sin (ωt + ϕ1) ..(i)

and θ2 = θ0 sin (ωt + ϕ2) ..(ii)

As it is given that amplitude and time period being equal but phases being different.

Now, for first pendulum at any time t

θ1 = θ0 (Right extreme)

From Eq. (i), we get

⇒ θ0 = θ0 sin (ωt + ϕ1)

Similarly, at the same instant t for pendulum second, we have

${θ}_{2} = - \dfrac{{θ}_{0}}{2}$

Note θ0 = 2o is the angular amplitude for the second pendulum the angular displacement is one degree therefore, ${θ}_{2} = \dfrac{{θ}_{0}}{2}$ and negative sign is taken to show for being left to mean position

From Eq. (ii), then

$- \dfrac{{θ}_{0}}{2} = {θ}_{0} \text\sin \left(ω t + {ϕ}_{2}\right)$

$\to \text\sin \left(ω t + {ϕ}_{2}\right) = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\to \left(ω t + {ϕ}_{2}\right) = - \dfrac{π}{6} \text{or} \dfrac{7 π}{6}$

$\text{or} \left(ω t + {ϕ}_{2}\right) = - \dfrac{π}{6} \text{or} \dfrac{7 π}{6} … \left(\text{iv}\right)$

From Eqs. (iv) and (iii), the difference in phases

$\left(ω t + {ϕ}_{2}\right) - \left(ω t + {ϕ}_{1}\right) = - \dfrac{7 π}{6} \text{or} \dfrac{π}{2} = \dfrac{7 π - 3 π}{6} = \dfrac{4 π}{6}$

$\text{or} \left({ϕ}_{2} - {ϕ}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{4 π}{6} = \dfrac{2 π}{3} = 1 2 {0}^{ο}$

questions.q: Infinite springs with force constants $k, 2k, 4kand8k \ldots..$ respectively are connected in series. The effective force constant of the spring will be
questions.solution:
Effective force constant is equal to the reciprocal of the sum of individual force constant, hence

$\dfrac{1}{{k}_{e}} = \dfrac{1}{{k}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{2}} + \dfrac{1}{{k}_{3}} + \ldots$

Given, ${k}_{1} = k, {k}_{2} = 2k, {k}_{3} = 3k, \ldots . .$

$∴\dfrac{1}{{k}_{e}} = \dfrac{1}{k} + \dfrac{1}{2k} + \dfrac{1}{4k} + \dfrac{1}{8k} + \ldots$

The given series a geometric progression series, hence sum is

${S}_{\infty} = \dfrac{a}{1 - r}$

where $a$ is first term of series and $r$ the common difference.

$⇒\dfrac{1}{{k}_{e}} = \dfrac{1}{k} \times \dfrac{1}{\left(1 - \dfrac{1}{2}\right)} = \dfrac{2}{k} ⇒ {k}_{e} = \dfrac{k}{2}$

Block is pushed toward the right by a distance $\dfrac{3l}{2}$ and released from rest. When block P is released from rest from a distance $\dfrac{3l}{2}$ toward right from mean position, this will be the amplitude of oscillation so velocity of block when passing from its mean position is given as
$v = A\omega = \dfrac{3l}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$
If mass m1 is added to it and just after if velocity of combined block becomes v1, from momentum conservation, we have
mv = (m + m1)v1
$∴ {v}_{1} = \dfrac{m}{m + {m}_{1}} ⋅ \dfrac{3l}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}}$

where A1 and ${\omega}_{1}$ are the new amplitude and angular frequency of SHM of the block.

Thus, the new amplitude of oscillation must be $l$ . So, we have,
$\dfrac{m}{m + {m}_{1}} ⋅ \dfrac{3l}{2}\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m}} = l\sqrt{\dfrac{k}{m + {m}_{1}}}$
On solving, we get
${m}_{1} = \dfrac{5}{4}m$
$∴ n = 5$

An ideal gas is enclosed in a vertical cylindrical container and supports a freely moving piston of mass $M$. The piston and the cylinder have an equal cross-sectional area $A$. Atmospheric pressure is ${p}_{0}$ and when the piston is in equilibrium, the volume of the gas is ${V}_{0}$. The piston is now displaced slightly from its equilibrium position. questions.solution:
& In equilibrium, pressure inside the cylinder = pressure just outside it

or & $\text{p} = {p}_{0} + \dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\text{A}}$

When piston is displaced slightly by an amount x, change in volume,

$\text{dV} = - \text{Ax}$

Since, the cylinder is isolated from the surroundings, nature of the process is adiabatic. In adiabatic process,

$\dfrac{\text{dp}}{\text{dV}} = - \gamma \dfrac{\text{p}}{\text{V}}$



or increase in pressure inside the cylinder,

$\text{dp} = - \dfrac{\left(\gamma \text{p}\right)}{\text{V}} \left(\text{dV}\right) = \gamma \left(\dfrac{{p}_{0} + \dfrac{\text{Mg}}{\text{A}}}{{V}_{0}}\right) \left(\text{Ax}\right)

This increase in pressure when multiplied with area of cross-section A will give a net upward force (or the restoring force). Hence,

\text{F} = - \left(\text{dp}\right) \text{A} = - \gamma \left(\dfrac{{p}_{0} A^{2} + \text{MgA}}{{V}_{0}}\right) \text{x}

Or \text{a} = \dfrac{\text{F}}{\text{M}} = - \gamma \left(\dfrac{{p}_{0} A^{2} + \text{MgA}}{{V}_{0} \text{M}}\right) \text{x}

Since, \text{a}$∝ - $\text{x}$,$ motion of the piston is simple harmonic in nature. Frequency of this oscillation is given by

\text{f} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\left|\dfrac{\text{a}}{\text{x}}\right|} = \dfrac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma \left({p}_{0} A^{2} + \text{MgA}\right)}{{V}_{0} \text{M}}}$
